I just received my copy of Zoroaster's Telescope from Ouroboros Press in Seattle. I went for the least expensive option, one of the 777 copies of the fabric-bound edition. They aren't numbered, though. Ah well.

Some few of you may know me from the oracle deck that I created, Elemental Hexagons (lame name, I know…), so the hexagon has long been a part of my occult interests. I had seen one or two diagrams from Zoroaster's Telescope almost a decade ago, the Great Mirror in particular, and had wanted more information about it.

It wasn't until 2013 that a translation was available in English. The diagrams are all still in German, being faithful reproductions of the original manuscript.

I've skimmed through it once already. I know it's going to take some deeper study and that I will also be making my own set of tiles to use with it. The most likely interaction between Zoroaster's Telescope and my deck of element-based cards will be to develop additional reading layouts. That's what I had in mind when I had first seen the Great Mirror diagram.

One reason why I think circumstances had me waiting until now before getting my hands on this book was that I wasn't fully ready for it. Not only does it claim to be rooted in Kabbala, the numbered tiles (99 of the 112 tiles) all have angelic correspondences. I've spent the last several years deeply studying the Golden Dawn grade rituals and the Kabbalistic Tree of Life. I think without those years of study, much of what is in Zoroaster's Telescope would have flown under my radar.

I believe that books and teachings come to us when we are ready and not before. Anyone else have that experience? What interesting esoteric books have you acquired lately, and do you have an idea as to why those books have come along when they did?
